$comment: T500 — declared state for the EPIC-026 stage register. Derived state (stage, readiness, next command) lives in the file tree and NEVER here; G-26-08 fails on a stage, readiness or next key at any depth (DF-7). This file is the only hand-authored input to the register, and therefore the only place the register can be lied to.
$listsExceptionsNotEpics: An Epic absent from `epics` is a delivery Epic with no posture, which is the common case. Twenty-eight entries repeating the default would be a second registration step, which FR-ESK-008 forbids. Keys are DIRECTORY NAMES, not EPIC-### labels — one identity, one spelling (DF-1).

002-team-review-access-storage.reason: Split 2026-08-07 by ruling D-19 into three module-aligned children. Holds their requirements, clarifications, SRS traceability and principle register; carries no tasks by design.

017-enhancement-model.reason: Split by ruling D-18 into four delivery children after ruling D-17 separated the product half from the repository process. Holds the spec, plan, research, data model, contracts and quickstart they share — the role _shared/ plays for the platform.

$waiverNote: None active. The DOR-08 waiver taken 2026-08-18 was RETIRED 2026-08-19 when T679 narrowed the condition to Constitution V's actual scope — the exception is gone because the reason for it is. A waiver covers exactly one DOR condition for one Epic, is owned by a programme role, carries a reason, and expires. It makes the Epic read 'Ready (waived)' and never plain 'Ready' — which is what stops an exception costing nothing. An expired waiver FAILS THE BUILD.
